features.optics-sfp-plus: 10G SFP+ SR, LR, ER, ZR (datasheet compatible transceiver types)

gaps.note: The datasheet's Physical list says '16 x 100M/ 1G SFP ports' and the HIG's Port Overview table says ports 4-19 are SFP at 100M/1G; the HIG's own Figure 5 callout over the same sixteen cages reads '16 x 2.5G SFP'. Same measure, same scope, two different answers, so this is a real conflict rather than two qualifiers. The group carries 1g because two independent tables agree on it and the third source is a figure callout, which the source-role table ranks below a spec table for anything but arrangement. A 2.5G-capable SerDes on a Qumran-UX is entirely plausible, so this may be a capability the tables under-state rather than an error in the figure.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or release note stating the SFP port speeds, or a NOS interface listing from a live unit

gaps.note: The rear face has five equal 52.4 mm slots on one pitch and only three fans. The outer two are drawn as decor plates because nothing in the intake gives them an identity: the accessory list has no filler part, the HIG's fan chapter never mentions a blank, and no figure shows one removed. They may be blanking covers with a part number, or they may be unopened stampings shared with the five-fan S9510-28DC, and a rectangle cannot tell you which. Drawn as panel rather than as two bays with no occupant, because an empty bay renders as a hole and would assert a slot the vendor never documents.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace accessory or spares list naming a fan blank, or a photograph of the rear with one of the outer plates removed

gaps.note: 'FAN' and the pointer-plus-numeral are drawn as chassis silkscreen because the numeral differs per position and a shared component skin cannot carry it, so in the render they are painted under the fan module and cannot be seen. Whether the metal actually prints them on the chassis or on each module's own bezel is not resolvable from the figures held: Fig 8's elevation shows them inside the module outline, Fig 22's inset shows only the badge and the screw, and no figure shows a bay with its module out at a readable size. The red 'E' badge and the thumbscrew ARE on the module - Fig 22 shows them together on the removed part - and are drawn there.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of an empty fan bay, or a fan module face photograph

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the five system lamps (GNSS, SYNC, STAT, FAN, PWR), the PSU FRU lamp, the Fan FRU lamp and the management jack's two lamps, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. The twenty-four green up/down arrows over the SFP columns and the eight corner lamps on the RJ45 block therefore keep their components' default of off/on rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Nine rows elsewhere in those same tables read 'Need NOS to activate this feature', so these may be NOS-defined rather than simply undocumented - which is a different fix, and the reason this is vendor-silent rather than nos-dependent: we do not know which, and guessing would put an answer where the unknown belongs.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: HIG section 8 says 'there are two locations on the case in which the grounding lug may be fixed' and the Figure 5 inset shows one, on the right flank just behind the front face. The second is named in no figure and reached by no photograph in the intake. Two lug positions are drawn side by side at that one documented location because the accessory lug takes two M4 screws; that is the mounting, not the second location.
gaps.wanted: a photograph or figure showing the second designated grounding location

gaps.note: No figure or photograph in the intake shows the underside at all, and the left flank only in perspective. Those two faces carry estimated content - three screw heads and a compliance sticker - drawn so the faces are not size-only, and their positions are not measurements.
gaps.wanted: straight-on photographs of the left flank and the underside

provenance.attrs: datasheet (Specifications / Performance / Environmental / Regulatory Compliance / Accessories) and HIG (port overview for reach, section 11 for the console settings, Installing an Antenna for the GNSS constellations and the active-antenna limits). Compliance transcribed verbatim, not tidied. The datasheet writes 'IEEE 1558v2' once in its key features and 'IEEE 1588v2' everywhere else; the corrected spelling is carried.
provenance.bottom: estimated - no figure or photograph in the intake shows the underside. The compliance sticker is the house convention (every shipped unit carries one) and its position is estimated. A bottom view mirrors LEFT and RIGHT, not front and back; the sticker is the only content and sits off-centre, so the mirror was applied rather than left to chance.
provenance.chassis: datasheet - '1 RU, 440 x 302 x 43.5mm', 'Weight: 4.44 kg or 9.79 lb (without FRU)', repeated verbatim by the HIG's Component Physical Information table. The 440 mm is the BODY and not a rack face: the HIG's Space Clearance section says the width 'is 17.32 inches (44cm) and shipped with a rack mount brackets suitable for 19 inch (48.3cm) wide racks', and the brackets are accessory item 3 at 50.4 x 43 x 20 mm each. Ears are therefore not drawn. Depth 302 is 'without the field replaceable units'; the HIG's Fig 5 top view dimensions the same body 302 mm and the unit over the PSU handles 327.4 mm, and states the fan handles project a further 25 mm.
provenance.fan-legends: figure-measured, and the one place on this device where WHAT IS PRINTED ON WHAT is genuinely unresolved. Each fan position carries, in a narrow strip at the right of its face, top to bottom: 'FAN', a left-pointing triangle with the bay number, a red 'E' airflow badge, a captive thumbscrew and a green lamp. The thumbscrew is the module's ('Loosen the captive screw located on the fan module', HIG section 6) and Fig 22's zoom inset shows the 'E' badge and that screw together on the module face, so both are drawn in ufispace/fan-402818-hc@1. The NUMERAL cannot be on the module - it differs per position - so 'FAN' and the pointer are chassis silkscreen here, drawn where the figure prints them, which puts them under the module and therefore invisible in the render. That is the s9510-28dc precedent (FAN-1..FAN-5, identically buried) rather than a decision this device makes for itself, and it is recorded as a gap rather than left to be discovered.
provenance.front-figure-scale: drawing - GATE 1 RUN ON BOTH FRONT FIGURES. HIG Fig 9 (fig-0014) draws the faceplate 1445 x 147 px for 440 x 43.5 mm: aspect 9.83 against a true 10.11, 2.8 % out, so it is orthographic enough to measure along a per-axis scale but not to a single one. The datasheet front elevation (fig-0002) is 1069 x 109 px, aspect 9.81, the same 2.9 % out. x positions below are measured on either at its own px/mm and the two agree to better than 0.5 mm on every feature checked (PSU lamps, LED column, all twelve SFP lamp pairs); y positions are the same measurements corrected for the 2.8 % vertical compression about the block centre. WHERE A STANDARD GOVERNS, THE STANDARD WINS: the figure draws each SFP aperture ~8 mm tall where SFF-8433 C02 is 10.40, which is the projection, not the metal.
provenance.ground-mark: figure-measured - the earth symbol is printed at the extreme right of the faceplate, x 432.7-438.7, centred y 21.9. It is a mark, not a connector: the bonding points are on the flank (HIG section 8), and this symbol is taken as pointing at them.
provenance.left: estimated - the left flank appears in the angle photo and in Fig 10 as plain metal with a perimeter screw line and the eight M4 tapped holes for the rack bracket. Three screw heads are drawn at estimated positions. AXIS: x = 0 is the REAR on a left view (viewer3d.js convention), so these positions are stated from the rear. Content is honestly sparse rather than blank.
provenance.lifecycle: searched 2026-08-28, 'UfiSpace S9501-28SMT end of life' - no announcement of any kind. The vendor's product page, FAQ page and datasheet are all live and the unit is actively marketed by resellers. none-announced is a real finding, not an omission.
provenance.mgmt-and-timing-jacks: figure-measured - four RJ45 housings, all sharing the port band's y extent 9.25-34.65. BITS is a single jack in a 16.5 mm shell (x 145.7-162.2, shell top 20.9 - it hangs low, unlike every other block); the OOB jack sits over the USB-A in one 17.3 mm shell (x 165.9-183.2); TOD sits over the IOIO console in one 16.05 mm shell (x 188.1-204.15). ORIENTATION READ AT 8x ZOOM ON fig-0002, jack by jack: BITS keyway DOWN, OOB keyway UP, TOD keyway UP, IOIO keyway DOWN - so each stacked pair mirrors, as ganged stacks do, and BITS (which is not in a stack) still points down. The measured vertical pitch inside both stacks is 13.9 mm, under the 16 mm std/rj45 bezel, so all six 8P8C jacks on this face are std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11) with their shells drawn as panel decor, per the s9510-28dc and m3000-14xc precedent. The OOB jack carries a green lamp at its top-left and an amber one at its top-right (colour-detected at x 168.3-171.4 and 179.5-182.2, y 14.9-17.3); semantics from the HIG Management port LED table. The vendor prints a network icon above the OOB jack and a USB trident below the USB socket rather than words; both are drawn as path marks.
provenance.part-numbers: none stated - neither the datasheet nor HIG R1.9 prints an orderable chassis SKU. The accessory lists name the FRUs only (PSU-201-DISB, PSU-201-AISB, FAN-402818-HC), which are the modules' own part numbers and live on their contracts. No SKU is invented here. Note that the S9510-28DC's chassis SKUs came from the owner rather than from any document, so their absence in the corpus is not evidence that none exist.
provenance.port-number-bands: figure-measured - every column's even port number is printed above the block and its odd number below, baselines y 9.0 and 36.7. For ports 4-19 the numerals sit straight on the dark faceplate; for 20-25 they sit on a dark blue painted band and for 26-27 on a light cyan one (RGB sampled 40,107,153 and 121,207,234; bands measured y 7.18-9.58 and 35.12-37.51). The bands are faceplate paint, so they are decor and the numerals are silkscreen - silkscreen paints over decor and under components, which is what keeps the numbers readable. The cyan band is how the hardware itself distinguishes the two MACsec ports from the other six SFP+.
provenance.port-speeds: datasheet and the HIG port-overview table AGREE and the HIG's own Figure 5 callout DISAGREES with both. Datasheet Physical: '16 x 100M/1G SFP ports', '8 x 1/10G SFP+ ports', '4 x 100M/1G RJ45 ports'. HIG Port Overview: ports 0-3 RJ45 100M/1G at 100 m, 4-19 SFP 100M/1G at 70 km, 20-25 SFP+ 1/10G at 80 km, 26-27 SFP+ 1/10G at 80 km. Figure 5's brackets instead read '16 x 2.5G SFP', '6 x 10G SFP+' and '2 x 10G SFP+ MACsec'. Two of the three callouts corroborate the tables (6 + 2 = 8 SFP+, and they are why the port table splits 20-25 from 26-27 at all); the 2.5G one contradicts two tables that agree, and is recorded as a sources-disagree gap with the tables carried. MACsec itself is not in dispute - the datasheet's key features list 'MACsec Support' and the cyan band on the faceplate marks the pair.
provenance.power: datasheet for the typical figure, HIG for the maximum, and they are not in conflict because they are different measures. Datasheet Environmental section: 'Typical power: 60 Watts (no transceiver)' - the scope is stated, which is rare and worth keeping. HIG Connecting Power, stated identically for the DC and the AC version: 'The maximum system power consumption is 96.9 watts', with no configuration or ambient named, so power-envelope is unstated rather than as-tested. Neither figure is reconciled against the sum of the modules, and no module draw is added to either. PSU inputs from the datasheet (AC 100-240 V 3 A, DC -36 to -75 V 8 A); per-PSU rating lives on the ufispace/psu-201-* contracts.
provenance.psu-bays: drawing and figure-measured - PSU0 face right edge at x 59.3, PSU1 right edge at 117.9 (both read as the right-hand hex vent field's edge on fig-0002), so with the 50.5 mm face from the HIG's Component Physical Information table the bays sit at x 8.8 and x 67.3, a 58.5 mm pitch. Cross-checked against the two green PSU status lamps, colour-detected at x 53.05 and 111.4 (58.35 mm apart) - the same pitch from an independent feature. Bay height 40.2 from the same table, y 1.6 (the face measured 2.2-40.3, i.e. centred to within the figure's resolution). Between the bays an 8 mm black divider strip printed, top to bottom, PSU0 / a left pointer / a right pointer / PSU1, all rotated 90 degrees - read at 14x on fig-0014 and confirmed on the angle photo, which shows all four marks unambiguously.
provenance.rear: figure-measured - HIG Fig 8 (fig-0013). THE REAR FIGURE'S ASPECT IS 9 % OUT (1382 x 149 px against 440 x 43.5), so only x is measured from it and y is proportional. Six deep vertical seams at x 19.1, 71.3, 123.8, 176.4, 228.6 and 280.8 divide the left two-thirds into FIVE slots of 52.2-52.6 mm on one pitch, of which the middle three hold fan modules and the outer two are blank plates. That is the same five-slot stamping the S9510-28DC uses for five fans, populated three-up here, which is consistent with the datasheet's '2+1 redundant Fans' and the HIG's '3 x Fan Modules' callout. The two blanks are drawn as decor plates rather than bays - see the blank-slot-identity gap. Right of the last seam a hex vent field runs to x 437.
provenance.right: drawing-fraction estimates - the Fig 5 grounding-lug inset shows this flank with the lug bolted to two tapped holes just behind the front face, between the PSU bay opening and the front edge; Fig 10 shows the bracket holes along the same flank. The inset is a perspective vignette with no scale, so the two lug positions are fractions of the depth, not measurements. AXIS: x = 0 is the FRONT on a right view (viewer3d.js convention). The HIG says there are TWO designated locations and shows one - see the second-grounding-location gap.
provenance.rj45-ports: figure-measured - ports 0-3 are a 2 x 2 ganged block in one white shell, x 209.1-240.4. Aperture columns measured 211.56-223.5 and 225.56-237.49 (centres 217.53 and 231.53, a 14.0 mm pitch); aperture rows 10.78-19.95 and 24.34-33.92 (centres 15.37 and 29.13, a 13.76 mm pitch). Both pitches are under 16 mm, so these are std/rj45-ganged as well. NUMBERING RUNS DOWN THE COLUMNS - 0 over 1, 2 over 3 - which is the vendor's own print, read off both front figures; the HIG port table's '0 ~ 3 RJ45 100M/1G' confirms only the range. Each jack carries a green lamp on its outer-left corner and an amber one on its outer-right; the top row's lamps are above the aperture and the bottom row's below, mirrored with the jacks (colour-detected at y 11.17-12.37 and 31.93-33.12).
provenance.sfp-block: figure-measured, then snapped to SFF-8433. Twelve columns in five ganged shells: 4-11 (x 243.6, 4 columns), 12-19 (x 304.7, 4 columns), 20-23 (x 365.85, 2), 24-25 (x 398.05, 1), 26-27 (x 416.15, 1) - shell edges read off fig-0002's light-grey border. THE COLUMN POSITIONS COME FROM THE LAMPS, NOT THE SHELLS, because the lamp pairs are a repeated feature of known spacing and therefore a ruler already in the picture: the twenty-four green arrows were colour-detected and their per-column midpoints give first-column origins of 244.18, 305.28, 366.43, 398.63, 416.73 and an in-shell pitch of 14.07-14.33 mm, which is the std/sfp-ganged 14.25 contract to 0.5 %. Cages are therefore placed at those origins on an exact 14.25 pitch, and every shell's computed right edge lands within 0.8 mm of the measured one. Rows: 10.40 tall on the 15.00 mm belly-to-belly pitch of std/sfp-ganged, centred on the measured shell centre 21.95, giving y 9.25 and 24.25. THE BOTTOM ROW IS MIRRORED (rotate: 180) - checked at 4x, the bails of both rows face the central lamp band. The lamp band itself is the shell's own metal showing between the rows and is not drawn separately; the shell is one silver decor rectangle behind the whole block, which is what the figure shows.
provenance.sources: datasheet (s9501-28smt-datasheet, converted) and the Hardware Installation Guide R1.9 (s9501-28smt-hig, converted, Figures 1-35), plus three vendor images: s9501-28smt-2-front.jpg and -3-rear.jpg (small straight-on renders, used for confirmation only) and s9501-28smt-1-angle.png (1602 x 627 three-quarter view, the only high-resolution image and the one that settled the PSU divider legends). No mechanical drawing of the chassis exists in the intake; the PSU has one (HIG Fig 6/7) and so does the top face (HIG Fig 5, top view).
provenance.status-leds: figure-measured - five lamps in one column, colour-detected on fig-0002 at x 136.2-138.7 with centres y 19.6, 21.95, 24.3, 26.7, 29.1, i.e. a 2.375 mm pitch and a 2.5 x 2.0 mm lamp. Labels printed dark on a white strip immediately to their right (x 139.9-144.5), reading GNSS SYNC STAT FAN PWR top to bottom - the same five and the same order the HIG's Front Panel LED tables give. DRAWN AT A 2.7 mm PITCH, NOT THE MEASURED 2.375: common/led-rect is 2.6 mm tall and cannot sit on a 2.375 pitch without overlapping its neighbour (L13), so the column is stretched 1.6 mm overall and re-centred on the measured centre 24.35. This is the same compromise, for the same reason, that ufispace/m3000-14xc records; the alternative was a new component for a lamp two devices share.
provenance.timing-block: figure-measured - three jacks in one column at x centre 127.1: 1PPS SMB centre y 9.25, 10MHZ SMB centre y 20.05, GNSS ANT SMA centre y 32.2, each labelled beneath its own jack (the S9510-28DC labels its to the left; this one does not). The drawn circles are 7.1, 6.9 and 10.5 mm across - the SMA reads larger than the SMBs, which is the correct relationship - but the jack outlines drawn here are common/smb-jack and common/sma-jack's own contract sizes, not these numbers: a round feature that measures two different diameters on a figure 2.8 % out in aspect is measuring the figure.
provenance.top: drawing - HIG Fig 5's top view is the only orthographic figure in the intake: 896 x 618 px for 440 x 302 mm, i.e. 2.036 and 2.046 px/mm, 0.5 % apart, so it passes Gate 1 on both axes and carries real geometry. Two long shallow channels run x 13.8-423.8 at y 47.0 (14.3 tall) and y 186.2 (15.1 tall); two rows of short channels, x 12.7-50.1 and 71.4-108.8, sit at y 109.5 and 269.3. Six lid screws were edge-detected at y 11.5, x 109.7 to 373.0 on a 52.7 mm pitch. AXIS: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house top-view convention; Fig 5 prints the front (PSU) edge at the bottom of the frame and these y values are measured from the top of it.
provenance.vents-front: figure-measured - one strip of triangular perforations across the top of the port area, x 212.0-430.5, y 1.6-6.4 (dark-pixel run on fig-0002). There is no vent field anywhere else on this face: the PSU hex fields belong to the PSU modules, not the panel.
